question: According to EU law1, for the movement of a pet animal to be considered as non-commercial, the pet animal must be accompanying its owner and the purpose of the movement must not be its sale or transfer of ownership. If the movement is carried out by an authorised person, it must take place within five days of the owner’s journey2. At the same time, the Commission is empowered to provide for derogations to this deadline3. 1.

On what up-to-date scientific risk assessment does the Commission base the assumption that the same properly vaccinated and documented pet from a listed non-EU country should be treated differently under animal health legislation if the five‑day deadline has been exceeded, compared to movement within this deadline (even though the animal health requirements remain unchanged), and does the Commission consider it proportionate that only private deferred transports – for example in cases of illness, flight cancellations or other force majeure – are, after a period of five days, effectively subject to the import regime including BCPs/TRACES?

Is the Commission considering proactively asking countries for applications in accordance with Article 13 of Regulation (EU) No 576/2013, and will the Commission make use of its empowerment to propose derogations or an extended deadline, for example 30 days, for cases that can be proven to be private and involve no transfer of ownership?
Article 4, point (14), of Regulation (EU) 2016/429. Article 245(2). Article 245(3) point (b)
answer: The non-commercial movement scheme was introduced in the EU legislation (1) to facilitate private movements of citizens with their pet animals. To prevent misuse of this scheme, specific criteria must be complied with for a movement to qualify as non-commercial. A key criterion is that the pet animal must accompany its owner.

When the non-commercial movement cannot be carried out by the owner and an authorised person travels with the animal instead, it was deemed proportionate to require that the pet animal movement remains close in time to that of the owner and no more than five days before or after that of the owner.

This requirement was originally established under Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 (2) and remains unchanged under Regulation (EU) 2016/429 (3) and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131 (4). The Commission does not plan to use the empowerment provided by Article 245(3), point (b), of Regulation (EU) 2016/429 to propose an extended period.
Finally, the Commission does not proactively ask non-EU countries to apply for listing under former Article 13 of Regulation (EU) No 576/2013 and now Article 17 of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/131.
